workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§172–176
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§172–176: Bo'orchu's Return, and the Retreat to the Qalqa
part: §§172–176 — Bo'orchu's Return, and the Retreat to the Qalqa
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§172–176, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Five sections after the first day of fighting. Chinggis Qahan musters his men at dawn and finds three missing; Bo'orchu comes in on a pack-horse he has found, and Boroqul brings Ögödei, wounded in the neck, whose blood he has sucked out with his own mouth (§§172–173). On the other side Wang Qan's men take Senggum off the field, and Achiq-Shirun and Wang Qan decide to withdraw (§174). Chinggis counts his 2,600, divides them along the two banks of the Qalqa, and loses Quildar, whose wounds are not yet healed, as he charges at game (§175); then he sends Jürchedei to the Ongirad, who submit (§176). Many passages are marked in the notes as first readings, in particular Bo'orchu's account at §172 and the speeches in §174.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Baižu qonožu üdür geiġülün bügüdgeġesü

morph.gloss: to stay the night, lodge [宿着]
to grow light, dawn (Ming 明) [敎明]
causative: make … (the e of the stem is lost before it)
to muster, count over, inspect (stem uncertain; compare bügüde 'all') [點視︀呵]

sentences.l: Standing, lodging, day brightening-ly, mustering-when,
sentences.i: We halted and spent the night, and when day broke and a check was made,
sentences.n: Read baižu qonožu as two converbs, 'standing (and) lodging' (Ming 立着 宿着, 'camped, spent the night'). The Ming 敎明 for geiġülün is 'cause to brighten', so 'day-breaking' is the sense; the stem geiġe- (its e lost before -ġül-) is as in the glossary. bügüdgeġesü is Ming 點視呵 'when (he) checked, looked over', the -ġesü 'when' ending (呵); the stem is uncertain and I connect it, tentatively, with bügüde 'all' (a roll-call). The sentence is cut here and the main clause follows in the next unit.

sentences.t: Ögödei, Boroγul, Boγ̇orču γurban ügei ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Boroqul, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Ögödei, Boroγul, Boγ̇orču, three, without, there-was.
sentences.i: Ögödei, Boroqul and Bo'orchu, the three, were missing.
sentences.n: Three names, then γurban 'three' (Ming 三箇) in apposition: the numeral follows the names it counts. ügei is 'without, there is not' with no copula; ažuγ̇u is a- 'be' + past -žuγ̇u (Ming 有來 'there was'), so 'three without there-was' is simply 'the three were not there'. Shiratori ends the sentence with the full stop after ažuγ̇u.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügü- lerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to speak; printed with a hyphen, first half of the split ügü-lerün [說]
verb-maker (second half of the split ügü-lerün; the Ming gloss is empty)

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan speaking:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: The word ügülerün is split across two printed words, ügü- | lerün (Ming 說). It is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün, the converb 'while speaking', which in this text introduces a speech. The two printed halves are carried here as one verb over two words.

sentences.t: "Ögödei-lüġe itegelten Boγ̇orču, Boroγul qojar qočorčuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名 一同]
reliance, trust (stem inferred from the Ming) [倚仗有的(每)]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Boroqul, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to be left behind [落後着有]

sentences.l: "Ögödei-with reliance-having-ones, Boγ̇orču, Boroγul, the two, left-behind-was.
sentences.i: "Bo'orchu and Boroqul, the two trusty men who were with Ögödei, have been left behind.
sentences.n: A speech begins. itegelten is Ming 倚仗有的 'those having reliance', the plural possessive -ten, here 'trust-having ones'; Ögödei-lüġe is 'with Ögödei' (Ming 一同). I read it as Bo'orchu and Boroqul, the two trusty men, who stayed behind with Ögödei; the line could also mean they relied on Ögödei's support, but the first reading fits the following unit. qočorčuγ̇u is Ming 落後着有 'was left behind' (-čuγ̇u after r).

sentences.t: Ažu ber üküžü ber jaγ̇u qaγačaqun tede" keġebe.
sentences.l: Living even, dying even, what parting, those" said.
sentences.i: Alive or dead, why should they be parted?" he said.
sentences.n: ažu ber üküžü ber is 'alive too, dead too' (Ming 存着 也 死着 也): two converbs each with the particle ber 'even, also'. qaγačaqun is Ming 相離 'parting'; the ending -qun is uncertain and the reading 'those who would part' is a first guess. jaγ̇u 'what' (Ming 如何) is used here as 'how, why'. tede is 'they, those', and the closing quotation mark falls after it, so the speaker is Chinggis, talking of the two men; the unit ends with keġebe 'said' (Ming 說了).

sentences.t: Bidan-uγ̇ai süni-de aγtas(i)-jan barižu qonožu

morph.gloss: ending of uncertain force: ours (Ming 咱的)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to stay the night, lodge [宿着]

sentences.l: Our night-at, geldings-own seizing, lodging,
sentences.i: We kept hold of our geldings that night and bedded down,
sentences.n: bidan-uγ̇ai is 'ours' (Ming 咱的); the ending -uγ̇ai is of uncertain force, so I give only 'ours'. aγtas(i)-jan has Shiratori's linking (i) before the reflexive-possessive -jan, 'one's own geldings' (Ming 騸馬每自的行); the Ming 行 is only its stock gloss. barižu qonožu is a two-converb chain, 'holding, lodging' (Ming 拿着 宿着), meaning they stayed the night with the horses in hand, ready.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan speaking:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: The same ügülerün as before, this time on a single printed word, introducing a speech.

sentences.t: "Qoināča bidan-u nekežü ireġesü qadqulduja"

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀牙 qadqulduja

morph.gloss: to fight (stem inferred from the Ming) [厮殺︀咱]

sentences.l: "From-behind, us-of attacking, coming-if, let-us-fight."
sentences.i: "If they come attacking us from behind, let us fight."
sentences.n: qoināča is 'from behind' (Ming 後行); nekežü is 'attacking' (Ming 襲着; the stem neke- elsewhere means 'pursue', so 'attack' is a stretch). bidan-u is 'of us', a genitive standing before a verb of action, as the Ming 咱的 has it: we should expect an accusative, so the case is a little odd. ireġesü is the 'if' form (Ming 來呵). qadqulduja is the hortative of 'fight together' (Ming 厮殺咱).

sentences.t: keġen žasažu baiba.

morph.gloss: to prepare, set in order [整治着]

sentences.l: saying, preparing, stood.
sentences.i: So saying, he set things in order and took his stand.
sentences.n: keġen closes the quotation (Ming 麽道, 'saying so'). žasažu baiba is a converb-plus-finite pair, 'preparing, stood' (Ming 整治着 立了): baiba 'stood' here carries the sense 'took his position'.

sentences.t: Üdür gegeġen bolγažu üžeġesü
sentences.l: Day light making, looking-when,
sentences.i: When day came and he looked,
sentences.n: Üdür gegeġen is 'day light' (Ming 日 明); bolγažu is the causative converb of bol- 'become' (Ming 敎做着, 'making it so'), so 'making day bright, i.e. at daybreak'. üžeġesü 'when he looked' (Ming 看呵). Shiratori runs this on without a stop, so the cut after 'looked' is mine.

sentences.t: qoināča nigen küġün aisu kürčü ireġesü Boγ̇orču ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: from-behind, one man coming, arriving, coming-if, Boγ̇orču was.
sentences.i: one man was seen coming up from behind, and when he arrived it was Bo'orchu.
sentences.n: The unit begins in mid-sentence from the previous: nigen küġün 'one man' (Ming 一箇 人), aisu 'coming' (Ming 來有; the ending is unclear, as the glossary notes), kürčü 'arriving'. Then ireġesü 'when he came' and ažuγ̇u 'it was' (Ming 有來), with the name Boγ̇orču in the subject slot and no copula. The glosses give a converb chain: coming, arriving, coming-if; I keep them as printed and unite them in one unit.

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču-ji kürčü ireġülüġed Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Boγ̇orču-ji arriving, having-made-come, Čiṅgis Qaγan speaking:
sentences.i: Bo'orchu, on arriving, was brought in, and Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Doubtful. Boγ̇orču-ji carries -ji, which the Ming glosses 行 and which may be accusative or dative; kürčü is 'arriving' and ireġülüġed is the causative 'having made come, having brought' (Ming 敎來了). I read the sense as Bo'orchu's arrival being brought to the Qahan, but who brought whom is not settled from the Ming alone.

sentences.t: "Müṅke teṅgeri medetügei" keġežü ebčeġü-ben mögeġeled- be.

morph.gloss: chest, breast (short form ebčeġü before the reflexive) [胷 自的行]
to strike, beat (stem inferred from the Ming 椎); the word is split in print, mögeġeled- + be [椎]
past: struck (second half of the split mögeġeled-be) [了]

sentences.l: "Eternal Heaven know!" saying, chest-own striking-did.
sentences.i: "Let eternal Heaven know!" he said, and struck his breast.
sentences.n: müṅke teṅgeri 'eternal Heaven' (Ming 長生 天) is the formula of oath and thanks. medetügei is the optative 'let (him) know' (Ming 知道者). ebčeġü-ben is 'chest-one's-own' (Ming 胷 自的行), the reflexive-possessive. The verb mögeġeled- | be is one word split over a line (Ming 椎 了, 'beat'): mögeġeled- is read here as 'strike, beat' (stem inferred from the Ming 椎) + past -be. The gesture is Chinggis's.

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Boγ̇orču speaking:
sentences.i: Bo'orchu said:
sentences.n: The same ügülerün, again introducing speech; the speaker is now Bo'orchu.

sentences.t: "Dobtulqui-dur morin(i)-jan unatala qaγdažu jabuγan güjižü jabuqui-dur

words.reading: 多卜禿勒(中灰)-突︀舌兒 Dobtulqui-dur

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to shoot (stem inferred from the Ming 射) [被射着]
to walk, go on foot [步行]
to run (stem inferred from the Ming 走) [走着]
dative-locative: at the going, when going

sentences.l: "Charging-at, horse-own falling, being-shot, on-foot running, going-at,
sentences.i: "In the charge my horse went down, shot, and as I ran on foot,
sentences.n: This is Bo'orchu's account, and the first reading of a hard passage. dobtulqui-dur is the participle 'charging' + dative-locative, 'at the charge' (Ming 衝時). morin(i)-jan is 'horse-own' with the Shiratori linking (i). unatala is Ming 倒(了) 'fallen', with -tala 'until, so that'. qaγdažu 'being shot' (Ming 被射着). jabuγan güjižü is 'on foot, running' (Ming 步行 走着). jabuqui-dur 'at the going' (Ming 行時). The unit stops at the comma of the chain.

sentences.t: mün Kereid Seṅgüm-ün deġere egeġer baiqui soγ̇or čolo-dur

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]
Senggum, a man's name (personal name) [人名的]
to turn back, wheel about (Ming 翻 'turn over'); here the bare stem, apparently used as a converb (uncertain) [翻着]
drawing into a fight, luring (noun or converb, uncertain; Ming 引鬭) [引鬭]
open space, gap (stem inferred from the Ming 空隙) [空隙裏]

sentences.l: just Kereid Seṅgüm-of upon turned-over standing luring-fight gap-in,
sentences.i: in the gap of the decoying fight, right by the Kereid of Senggum, who stood wheeling about,
sentences.n: The hardest unit in the section, and offered only as a first reading. mün is 'just, the very' (Ming 只); Kereid Seṅgüm-ün deġere is 'upon (the) Kereid of Senggum' (Ming 種名 人名的 上; whether the genitive belongs to Kereid or to deġere is not settled). egeġer baiqui is Ming 翻着 立的 'standing turned over'; I read egeġerü- as 'turn back' (as in egeġerčü at §174), here as a bare stem (uncertain). soγ̇or is Ming 引鬭 'luring into a fight', and čolo-dur is Ming 空隙裏 'in a gap, an opening'. I take it that Bo'orchu was running through an opening beside Senggum's Kereid, who were wheeling about. Do not rely on the construction of the whole phrase.

sentences.t: ačiγ̇atu morin ačiγ̇a-ban kebeligülžü bain büküi-ji

morph.gloss: to tilt, slant (stem inferred from the Ming 歪) [歪了着]

sentences.l: load-having horse, load-own tilted, standing being-one,
sentences.i: a horse with a load, its load tilted sideways, the one standing there,
sentences.n: ačiγ̇atu morin is 'a horse having a pack' (Ming 䭾䭾有的 馬), the possessive -tu. ačiγ̇a-ban kebeligülžü is 'its own load having tilted' (Ming 歪了着), a causative converb. bain büküi-ji is 'standing, who is' (Ming 立 有的 行), and the ending -ji (accusative, uncertain) makes the whole phrase an object, but the verb that governs it is not in this unit (no verb of finding is printed); the next unit cuts the load, not the horse.

sentences.t: ačiγ̇a in-ü hoγtolžu iṅgirčaγ-tur in-ü unužu γarču

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to cut off, sever (stem inferred from the Ming 割斷) [割斷着]

words.reading: 影吉舌兒察黑-途舌兒 iṅgirčaγ-tur

morph.gloss: single saddle, pad saddle (reading uncertain) [單鞍 行]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: load its cutting-off, single-saddle-on its riding, going-out,
sentences.i: I cut its load free, mounted it on its single saddle, and rode out,
sentences.n: ačiγ̇a in-ü hoγtolžu is 'its load cutting off' (Ming 割斷着); in-ü is the genitive 'his, its'. iṅgirčaγ-tur is Ming 單鞍 行 'on a single saddle', the reading of the first word uncertain. unužu 'riding' (Ming 騎着) and γarču 'going out' (Ming 出着). A three-converb chain in which the finite verb waits for the next unit.

sentences.t: bidan-u qaγačaqu. γaruγsan mör müdkin jabužu olžu edüi irebe. bi" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to tread, trample (stem inferred from the Ming 踏) [踏着]
so much, only this much (adverb) [方纔]

sentences.l: our parted going-out track treading, going, finding, just-now came, I" said.
sentences.i: treading the track on which we had parted and gone out, going along it and finding it, I have only now come." So he said.
sentences.n: bidan-u qaγačaqu γaruγsan mör is 'the track where we parted and went out' (Ming 咱的 離的 出了的 路), the participles qaγačaqu and γaruγsan both before mör 'track'. müdkin jabužu olžu is 'treading, going, finding' (Ming 踏着 行着 得着). edüi irebe 'just now came' (Ming 方纔 來了). bi is the 'I' (Ming 我) and the quotation mark closes at it; keġebe 'said' ends the speech. This unit gathers the end of a long chain; the closing 'bi keġebe' is the narrator's wrap-up of the speech.

sentences.t: Basa Qorumud atala
sentences.l: Again, little-while staying,
sentences.i: Again, after a short while,
sentences.n: basa 'again' (Ming 再), qorumud 'a little while' (Ming 少頃), atala 'while staying' (Ming 住間): a- 'be, stay' with -tala 'until, while' (as in the glossary).

sentences.t: basa nigen küġün aisu kürčü aisuqui-dur

words.reading: 阿亦速中灰-突︀舌兒 aisuqui-dur

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the coming, when coming

sentences.l: again one man coming, arriving, coming-at,
sentences.i: another man came, and as he drew near,
sentences.n: basa nigen küġün aisu kürčü aisuqui-dur is 'again one man coming, arriving, at the coming' (Ming 再 一 人 來有 到着 來時). The same aisu (Ming 來有) as in §172; aisuqui-dur adds the participle -qui and the dative-locative -dur, 'when coming'.

sentences.t: doro in-ü köl(i)-jen unžižažu aisu üžeġesü

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to hang down, dangle (stem inferred from the Ming 垂) [垂着]

sentences.l: below his legs-own hanging, coming, looking-when,
sentences.i: his legs hanging down below as he came, and when Chinggis looked,
sentences.n: doro 'below' (Ming 下), in-ü köl(i)-jen 'his own legs' (Ming 他的 腳 自的行), with Shiratori's linking (i) and the reflexive-possessive -jen; unžižažu 'hanging down' (Ming 垂着, stem inferred). aisu again, then üžeġesü 'when he looked' (Ming 看呵). The viewpoint is Chinggis's.

sentences.t: γaγča küġün metü bijü.
sentences.l: alone man like there-is.
sentences.i: he seemed to be one man alone.
sentences.n: γaγča küġün metü bijü, 'a single man like there-is' (Ming 獨 人 般 有): metü 'like' follows its noun; bijü is bü- 'be' + -jü, 'is, there is'. There is nothing in the Mongol to say the man is two, but the next unit shows he is.

sentences.t: Iren baraγ̇asu Ögödei- jin qoināča Boroγul sundulažu

morph.gloss: to end, be finished; here an auxiliary: when done [了呵]
Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
genitive: of (after a vowel; second half of the split Ögödei- + jin) [的]
Boroqul, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to ride double (stem inferred from the Ming 㬪騎) [㬪騎着]

sentences.l: Coming-finished-when, Ögödei-of from-behind Boroγul riding-behind,
sentences.i: When he had come up, there was Boroqul, riding double behind Ögödei,
sentences.n: iren baraγ̇asu is 'coming, when finished' (Ming 來 了呵): bara- 'finish' is an auxiliary 'when it had come'. The name Ögödei- | jin is split across two printed words (Ming 人名 的): the genitive -jin is the form after a vowel; Ögödei-jin qoināča is 'from behind Ögödei'. sundulažu is Ming 㬪騎着 'riding double, behind another' (stem inferred). So the 'lone man' was two on one horse.

sentences.t: aman-u žabažin(i)-jar čisun čuburiγ̇ulžu kürčü irebe.

morph.gloss: lip, edge of the mouth (stem inferred from the Ming 脗) [脗 依着]
instrumental: along, by (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to trickle, flow in drops (stem inferred from the Ming 流) [流着]

sentences.l: mouth-of lip-along blood dripping, arriving came.
sentences.i: blood running along the lips of his mouth, he came up.
sentences.n: aman-u is 'of the mouth' (Ming 口約) and žabažin(i)-jar is Ming 脗依着 'along the lips', an instrumental after the stem. čisun čuburiγ̇ulžu is Ming 血 流着 'blood making flow, dripping'. The finite verb is kürčü irebe, 'arriving, came' (Ming 到着 來了). The reason for the blood is given in the next unit.

sentences.t: Ögödei sužijasu-ban sumun-a tusdažu čisun in-ü qaγdarun

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the vein of the neck (Ming 項脈 'neck vein') [項脈 自的行]
to strike, hit (stem inferred from the Ming 被著) [被著︀着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to congeal, clot (stem inferred from the Ming 凝) [被凝的]

sentences.l: Ögödei neck-own arrow-to being-struck, blood his clotting;
sentences.i: Ögödei had been struck in the neck by an arrow, and his blood had clotted.
sentences.n: sužijasu-ban is 'neck(-vein) one's own' (Ming 項脈 自的行). sumun-a is the arrow with the dative ending (Ming 箭行), 'by the arrow'; tusdažu is Ming 被著着 'being hit' (stem inferred). qaγdarun is Ming 被凝的 'clotted': the stem qaγdar- is inferred from the Ming and the final -un is uncertain. Shiratori does not break here; the cut is mine.

sentences.t: Boroγul ama-γ̇ar(i)-jan simižu böglegsen čisun žabažin(i)-jar čuburiγ̇ulžu irebe.

morph.gloss: Boroqul, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to suck (stem inferred from the Ming 咂) [咂着]
to clog, clot (stem inferred from the Ming 塞) [塞了的]
lip, edge of the mouth (stem inferred from the Ming 脗) [脗 依着]
instrumental: along, by (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to trickle, flow in drops (stem inferred from the Ming 流) [流着]

sentences.l: Boroγul mouth-own-with sucking, clotted blood lips-along dripping, came.
sentences.i: Boroqul, sucking the clotted blood with his own mouth, came with the blood running down his lips.

sentences.l: "Wang-Qan son-own Seṅgüm-i arrow-with red cheek falling shot,
sentences.i: "Wang Qan's own son Senggum, shot in the red cheek with an arrow, so that he fell,
sentences.n: Doubtful throughout the speech. Waṅ-Qān opens the report and is its subject; köġü-ben Seṅgüm-i is 'his own son Senggum' (Ming 子 自的 人名行), reflexive-possessive. The Ming glosses are učuma-γ̇ar 射名敎 'with a shot' (instrumental), eṅgesge qačar 紅 腮 'red cheek' (the first word may be 'rosy'; uncertain), unatala qaγdažu 倒了 被射着 'falling, being shot'. The Ming is a string of nouns and converbs; I treat the reflexive (Wang Qan's own son) as the sign that Wang Qan is the subject of the verbs that follow (turning, speaking), reported here by Qada'an-Daldurqan.

sentences.n: Ačiγ-Širun-u is the genitive of the name; ene üge-dür is 'at this word' (Ming 這 言語 裏).

sentences.t: "Že; tein böġesü köġün alžaγ̇üžai; köġün-i ülü deṅselgen asaradqun

morph.gloss: to be wearied, be harmed (stem inferred from the Ming 恐勞) [恐勞]
to jolt, shake (stem inferred from the Ming 搖動) [搖動]
to raise, bear, care for (Ming 擡擧) [擡擧你每]

sentences.l: "Agreed; so being-if, son lest-tired; son-i not jolting, raise-you,"
sentences.i: "Agreed. If it is so, the son may be worn out; carry the son, all of you, without jolting him,
sentences.n: Že is Ming 應許 'assent'. tein böġesü is 'so being, if it be' (Ming 那般 有呵). alžaγ̇üžai is Ming 恐勞 'lest he be tired'; the stem and ending are inferred from the Ming. köġün-i 'the son' as object, ülü deṅselgen is 'not jolting' (Ming 不 搖動), asaradqun the plural imperative of asara- 'raise' (Ming 擡擧你每).

sentences.t: kēġed qadqulduγsan γažar-ača qarin ičuba" keġebe.

morph.gloss: converb of completed action: having said (long vowel kē- as printed)

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀黑三 qadqulduγsan

morph.gloss: to fight (stem inferred from the Ming 厮殺) [厮殺︀了的]
to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred from the Ming 退) [退了]

sentences.l: saying, fought-place-from back withdrew" said.
sentences.i: and, saying so, they drew back from the place where they had fought." So he said.
sentences.n: kēġed is 'having said' (Ming 說了). qadqulduγsan γažar-ača is Ming 厮殺了的 地處 'from the place where they fought'. qarin ičuba is Ming 囘 退了 'back withdrew'. Shiratori's closing quotation mark comes after ičuba, which puts the withdrawal inside the speech; the sense is that Wang Qan's side retired, and the narration and the speech have run together.

sentences.t: Tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan Dalan-Nemürges(e)-eče Qalqa huruγ̇u ködölürün toγ̇o toγ̇olalduba.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

words.reading: 荅闌-捏木舌兒格薛-額徹 Dalan-Nemürges(e)-eče

glyphs.s: 荅闌-捏木舌兒格薛-額徹

morph.gloss: Dalan-Nemürges, a place (Ming 地名) [地名 處]
the Qalqa river (Ming 河名) [河名]

sentences.l: From-there Čiṅgis Qaγan, from-Dalan-Nemürges, Qalqa along moving, count counted.
sentences.i: From there, as Chinggis Qahan moved along the Qalqa from Dalan-Nemürges, they took a count.
sentences.n: Tendēče 'from there' (Ming 自那裏), with the long ē as printed; Dalan-Nemürges(e)-eče is 'from Dalan-Nemürges' with the bracketed vowel (Ming 地名 處). Qalqa is a river name here (Ming 河名); huruγ̇u is Ming 順 'following, down along'. toγ̇o toγ̇olalduba is a noun and verb from one root, 'counted a count' (Ming 數 共數了), the reciprocal -ldu- here 'together, all of them'.

sentences.t: Toγ̇olalduγ̇asu qojar miṅγan žirγoγ̇an žaγ̇ud bolba.
sentences.l: Counting-when two thousand six hundreds became.
sentences.i: The count came to two thousand six hundred.
sentences.n: toγ̇olalduγ̇asu 'when they counted' (Ming 共數呵) then the numerals in order: qojar miṅγan žirγoγ̇an žaγ̇ud 'two thousand six hundred' (Ming 兩 千 六 百). žaγ̇ud is the plural 'hundreds'. bolba is 'became' (Ming 做了).

sentences.t: Nigen miṅγan γurban žaγ̇ud Čiṅgis Qaγan Qalqa-jin höreneži eteġed(i)-jer neġübe.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
the Qalqa river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
instrumental: along (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)

sentences.l: One thousand three hundreds, Čiṅgis Qaγan, Qalqa-of west sides-along moved-camp.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan moved camp along the west side of the Qalqa with thirteen hundred.
sentences.n: nigen miṅγan γurban žaγ̇ud is 'one thousand three hundreds' (Ming 一 千 三 百), 1300. höreneži is Ming 西 'west' (Shiratori's spelling; the exact stem is uncertain); eteġed(i)-jer is Ming 邊依着 'along the side', plural eteġed + linking (i) + instrumental -jer. The numeral stands before the leader's name, a little unusual.

sentences.t: Nigen miṅγan γurban žaγ̇ud Qalqa-jin doronaži eteġed(i)-jer Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud neġübe.

morph.gloss: the Qalqa river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
instrumental: along (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
the Uruqud, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]
the Mongqud, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]

sentences.l: One thousand three hundreds, Qalqa-of east sides-along, Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud, moved-camp.
sentences.i: Thirteen hundred, the Uruqud and the Mongqud, moved camp along the east side of the Qalqa.
sentences.n: The same pattern mirrored: doronaži is Ming 東 'east'. Uruγ̇ud and Moṅγud are Ming-glossed as 種名 (names of peoples) and stand in apposition to the thousand three hundred, since the verb neġübe 'moved camp' (Ming 起了) governs them. So the two halves of the 2,600 are split by river.

sentences.t: Tein neġüžü aisuqui-dur

words.reading: 阿亦速(中灰)-突︀舌兒 aisuqui-dur

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the coming, when coming

sentences.l: So moving-camp, at-coming,
sentences.i: Moving camp in this way, as they came along,
sentences.n: tein 'so' (Ming 那般), neġüžü 'moving camp' (Ming 起着), aisuqui-dur 'at the coming' (Ming 來時). A two-converb opening.

sentences.t: künesün-e abalan jabuqui-dur

morph.gloss: to hunt in a drive (Ming 打圍) [打圍]
dative-locative: at the going, when going

sentences.l: for-food hunting, at-going,
sentences.i: and hunting for food as they went,
sentences.n: künesün-e 'for food, provisions' (Ming 糧行) with the dative, abalan 'hunting in a drive' (Ming 打圍), jabuqui-dur 'at the going' (Ming 行時). This unit and the one before are two converb-with-time phrases, set up for the main clause.

sentences.t: Quildar jaras(i)-jan anaγ̇ai üdüġüj-e

morph.gloss: Quildar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
wound, scar (Ming 傷痕) [傷痕(每)自的(行)]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
to heal, recover (stem inferred from the Ming 痊可) [痊可]

sentences.l: Quildar wounds-own healed not-yet
sentences.i: Quildar's wounds had not yet healed,
sentences.n: jaras(i)-jan is 'wounds, one's own' (Ming 傷痕 自的行), anaγ̇ai is Ming 痊可 'recovered' (ending uncertain), and üdüġüj-e is 'not yet' (Ming 未行) with -e; the j is a glide. The reading of the clause is plain; the unit is the setup of what follows.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a idqaγ̇asu ülü bolun

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to urge, advise (stem uncertain; Ming 勸) [勸呵]

sentences.l: to-Čiṅgis Qaγan urging-when, not willing,
sentences.i: and when the Qahan urged him, he would not consent,
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a idqaγ̇asu ülü bolun is Ming 皇帝行 勸呵 不 肻: 'when advised, not consenting'. Doubtful which is the adviser: the dative Qaγan-(n)a would normally name the one to whom advice is given. I take 'urged' as Chinggis's urging and ülü bolun as Quildar's refusal (the Ming 肻 is 'consent').

sentences.t: göreġesün-dür dobtulqu bolun hügderežü nögčibe.

words.reading: 戈舌劣額孫-突︀舌兒 göreġesün-dür

morph.gloss: game animals, wild beasts (Ming 走獸) [走獸 行]
to spur on, set off again (stem inferred from the Ming 重發) [重發着]
to pass on, pass away (stem inferred from the Ming 過去) [過去了]

sentences.l: game-at charging-ones becoming, spurring, passed-on.
sentences.i: and, charging at the game, spurred on, he passed on.
sentences.n: göreġesün-dür is Ming 走獸 行 'at the beasts'. dobtulqu bolun is Ming 衝的 做, 'becoming a charger'; hügderežü is Ming 重發着 (stem inferred) 'urging the horse on again'. nögčibe is Ming 過去了 'passed away': a euphemism for death. The next unit, with the placing of his bones, confirms it, though the Ming alone gives only 'went by, passed on'.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan Qalqa-jin Ornuγ̇u-jin kelteġei

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
the Qalqa river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
Ornu'u, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名的]

sentences.l: There Čiṅgis Qaγan, Qalqa-of Ornuγ̇u-of half-
sentences.i: There, Chinggis Qahan, midway on Ornu'u of the Qalqa,
sentences.n: Ornuγ̇u-jin is Ming 山名的 'of the mountain named Ornu'u'. kelteġei is Ming 半 'half'; I take it as a ledge or midway slope, the unit continuing into the next. The two genitives Qalqa-jin Ornuγ̇u-jin are placed in a row, possessor before possessed.

sentences.t: qada-da jasun in-ü tabiγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to put, set down (a spelling of talbi-) [敎放了]

sentences.l: cliff-on, bones his caused-to-be-set.
sentences.i: had his bones laid on the cliff.
sentences.n: qada-da is 'cliff-on' (Ming 崖行). jasun in-ü is 'bone his' (Ming 骨殖 他的), and tabiγ̇ulba is the causative 'caused to be set down' (Ming 敎放了) of tabi- (talbi-). 'His' is Quildar's. The Ming tells nothing of a ceremony; the plain sense is that the body was laid on the ledge.

sentences.t: Qalqa-jin Büjür naγ̇ur-tur čidququ hužaγ̇ur-a

morph.gloss: the Qalqa river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
Lake Büyür (Ming 海子名) [海︀子名]
to pour, flow in (stem inferred from the Ming 注) [注的]

sentences.l: Qalqa-of Büjür lake-into pouring root-to,
sentences.i: To the root of the Qalqa, where it pours into Lake Büyür,
sentences.n: Büjür is Ming 海子名 'name of a lake', and naγ̇ur-tur is Ming 海子 行 'into the lake'. čidququ is Ming 注的 'that pours'; hužaγ̇ur-a is Ming 根源行 'to the source, root'. The root hužaγ̇ur is used of the end of a river here (the Qalqa's mouth); the verb comes two units on.

sentences.t: Terge, Emel-ten Uṅgirad bi keġen medežü

morph.gloss: Terge, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Emel, a man's name (personal name) [人名等]
the Ongirad, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]
is, there is (short form of bü-; compare bijü) [有]

sentences.l: Terge, Emel-and-others Uṅgirad is saying, knowing,
sentences.i: knowing that the Ongirad of Terge, Emel and others were there,
sentences.n: Terge and Emel-ten are names (Ming 人名, 人名等); -ten is Ming 等 'and the like', the same ending as in itegelten. Uṅgirad is Ming 種名. bi keġen medežü is 'there is, saying, knowing' (Ming 有 麽道 知着): the speech-closing keġen here marks a quoted thought, 'knowing that …'.

sentences.t: Žürčede-ji uruγ̇ud(i)-jar ilebe.

morph.gloss: Jürchedei, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]

words.reading: 兀舌魯兀的-牙舌兒 uruγ̇ud(i)-jar

morph.gloss: the Uruqud, a people [(種名)領着]
instrumental: with (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)

sentences.l: Žürčede-ji Uruγ̇ud-with sent.
sentences.i: he sent Jürchedei with the Uruqud.
sentences.n: Žürčede-ji is the name with -ji, here an accusative, 'Jürchedei (object)'. uruγ̇ud(i)-jar is Ming (種名) 領着 'leading the Uruqud': the Shiratori (i) before the instrumental -jar, 'with the Uruqud'. ilebe is Ming 敎去了 'sent'.

sentences.t: Ilerün Uṅgirad irgen erte üdür-eče

morph.gloss: the Ongirad, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]

sentences.l: Sending, Uṅgirad people from-early day
sentences.i: As he sent him, the Ongirad people from olden days
sentences.n: ilerün is Ming 去時 'at the going'; I take ile- as 'to send, go' with the -rün of time. Uṅgirad irgen is 'Ongirad people' (Ming 種名 百姓), erte üdür-eče 'from early days' (Ming 在前 日子 行). The unit is a setting.

sentences.t: že-jin žisü-ġer ökin-ü oṅge-ġer kēġesü elsed-že;

morph.gloss: nephew, sister's son (Ming 外甥) [外甥的]
form, appearance (Ming 容貌) [容貌 依着]
colour, face (Ming 顏色) [顏色 依着]
conditional converb: when, if (long vowel kē- as printed)
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降) [投降 也者︀]

sentences.l: nephew-of appearance-by, girl-of colour-by, saying-when, let-us-submit;
sentences.i: by the looks of the sister's son, by the colour of the daughter, so it is said, let us submit;
sentences.n: Doubtful. že-jin žisü-ġer ökin-ü oṅge-ġer is Ming 外甥的 容貌依着 女的 顏色依着 'by the appearance of a sister's son, by the colour of a girl'. The Ongirad were the people who gave Mongol men their wives, so this seems to be an appeal to kinship by marriage. kēġesü 'when it is said' (Ming 說呵), and elsed-že 'let us submit' (Ming 投降 也者). The speaker is not named; I read it as a saying of the Ongirad themselves, and the 'we' of the next unit as the same speakers.

sentences.t: müd bulγa in-ü kēġesü qadquldud-že bida keġežü ileġesü

morph.gloss: they, those (uncertain; Ming 他每) [他每]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: they revolt his saying-when, let-us-fight, we saying, sending-when,
sentences.i: if they say "revolt," let us fight, we, so saying; and when it was sent,
sentences.n: müd bulγa in-ü kēġesü is Ming 他每 反 他的 說呵 'if (it) is said of them, revolt'. qadquldud-že 'let us fight' (Ming 厮殺 也者), bida keġežü 'we, saying'. ileġesü is Ming 去了 and is the 'when' form of ile- (the same root as ilebe). What was sent is not said, and the speaker is not named (see the previous unit).

sentences.t: Žürčedei-dür elsen orožuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 主舌兒扯歹-突︀舌兒 Žürčedei-dür

morph.gloss: Jürchedei, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降) [投降]

sentences.l: Žürčedei-to submission entered.
sentences.i: they submitted to Jürchedei.
sentences.n: Žürčedei-dür is 'to Jürchedei' (Ming 人名行). elsen orožuγ̇ui is Ming 投降 入了, 'submission entered, submitted': else- 'submit' (stem inferred from the Ming 投降) with the converb -n, and oro- 'enter' with -žuγ̇ui.

sentences.t: Elsen oroγdažu Čiṅgis Qaγan jaγ̇u ber an-u ese kündebe.

morph.gloss: to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降) [投降]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
their (back-vowel companion of in-ü, third-person genitive set after its noun) [他的]
to disturb, touch, move (Ming 動; reading uncertain) [動了]

sentences.l: Submission being-entered, Čiṅgis Qaγan anything-even their not disturbed.
sentences.i: Once they had submitted, Chinggis Qahan did not touch anything of theirs.
sentences.n: Elsen oroγdažu is 'submission being entered' (Ming 投降 被入着), oro- with the passive -γda-. jaγ̇u … ber … ese is 'anything-even … not' (Ming 甚麽 也 … 不曾), a pattern of negation like 'not anything'. an-u is Ming 他的 'their'; kündebe is Ming 動了, 'touched, disturbed' (uncertain). ese negates a past act.
